text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The 1,000-megawatt reactor number six at Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant will not start operating at the beginning of November as planned due to delayed deliveries of Russian nuclear fuel, plant officials said.
-- Bulgaria's first voucher privatisation tender scheduled to start on Monday will be postponed because of a shortage of documentation kits, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- The European Bank for Investment and Development (EBRD) plans to start implementaion of projects worth 300 million Ecu in Bulgaria with the participation of several foreign investors, EBRD said in a strategy blueprint for Bulgaria sent to the cabinet.
-- Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry prepares a barter deal with Kazakhstan for wheat imports in exchange for canned food, ministry officials said.
-- Finance minister Dimitar Kostov said pegging the lev to a foreign currency or introducing a fixed exchange rate would be counterproductive amid the current crisis in Bulgaria's banking sector.

-- Bulgarians could be able to draw their deposits from a bank put under special supervision seven months after the central bank opens an insolvency procedure against such bank, under drafr amendments to the Deposit Guarantee Law, approved by the parliament's budget committee.
-- Bulgaria's consumer price inflation for September and for October will be less than 20 percent, a National Statistics Institute forecast said.
-- Finance minister Dimitar Kostov said the ratings assigned to Bulgaria by Moody's Investor's Service had no serious weight as the country did not currently plan to place issues on global markets.
